news.story_lead: 4 suspected infiltrators killed in landmine blast along LoC in J&K's Poonch The deceased were identified as JKLF Poonch president Faizan Sagheer, Ishtiaq, Asim Rafiq, and Waqas Sharif. At least four men, purportedly infiltrators, were reportedly killed in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast along the Line of Control (LoC) in Krishna Ghati (KG) sector of Poonch district on Monday, said people familiar with the development. “A group of four infiltrators was reportedly eliminated in a powerful IED blast in Salotri area near Nangi Tekri along the LoC in Poonch sector on Monday afternoon,” official sources told HT.

At least four men, purportedly infiltrators, were reportedly killed in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast along the Line of Control (LoC) in Krishna Ghati (KG) sector of Poonch district on Monday, said people familiar with the development. “A group of four infiltrators was reportedly eliminated in a powerful IED blast in Salotri area near Nangi Tekri along the LoC in Poonch sector on Monday afternoon,” official sources told HT. The area is being manned by soldiers of the 7 Jat Regiment. Pakistan media handles' claims While the Indian Army hasn’t yet issued any statement on the incident, some Pakistan media handles on X claimed that four men were killed in a landmine explosion in Mahandala village, Hajira, near the Line of Control (LoC), while repairing a spring-water pipeline. The deceased were identified as JKLF Poonch president Faizan Sagheer, Ishtiaq, Asim Rafiq, and Waqas Sharif, all residents of Mandla, in Tehsil Hajira, district Poonch (PoJK). However, heavy rainfall can sometimes wash away the landmines, causing them to surface in areas where they may pose a potential risk. It also remained unclear whether the group comprised suspected terrorists attempting to cross the LoC, or Pakistan security personnel patrolling the area. news.headline: ‘Drank at 3 bars, drove Mini Cooper at 120 km/hr’: Teen driver's friends nabbed day after crash kills 3 in Kochi
news.story_lead: ‘Drank at 3 bars, drove Mini Cooper at 120 km/hr’: Teen driver's friends nabbed day after crash kills 3 in Kochi Police said two youngsters who were in the car at the time of the accident have been arrested and charged with abetting. The Keralam police arrested two more persons on Monday in connection with the Mini Cooper car crash case, while the family of one of the victims demanded that murder charges be invoked against 19-year-old Suhail Sajeev, who drove the luxury car that rammed into a scooter and killed three persons. In the early hours of October 11, a speeding black Mini Cooper, driven by Suhail, rammed into the back of a scooter while navigating a curve on the road leading to the Cochin International Airport near Nedumbassery.

In the early hours of October 11, a speeding black Mini Cooper, driven by Suhail, rammed into the back of a scooter while navigating a curve on the road leading to the Cochin International Airport near Nedumbassery. Suhail, who the police confirmed was drunk at the time, was apprehended by locals and handed over to the police. Iyas, Devika and Gopika, all in their early 20s, travelling on the scooter, succumbed to injuries at nearby hospitals. Two absconding boys nabbed Officials at the Nedumbassery police station, where the FIR was registered, said two youngsters who were in the car at the time of the accident have been arrested and charged with abetting. They had escaped from the scene of the car crash following the incident and were apprehended from Alappuzha district. Earlier, Suhail and his friend Ninav had been arrested by the police and produced before a magistrate who remanded them to the Borstal school in Thrikkakara where remand prisoners between 18 and 21 are lodged. Suhail has been booked for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Police are likely to file an application in court demanding their custody for questioning. ‘Drank at 3 bars, drove at 120 km/hr’ Police have found that Suhail and his friends had visited at least three bars in Kochi on October 10 and consumed alcohol before going to the airport to pick up their friend. The Mini Cooper, that Suhail was driving, was speeding at 120 km/hr at the time of the crash, officials have found. The Excise department has launched an inquiry against the three bars for serving alcohol to Suhail and Ninav. As per Excise rules, establishments are barred from serving liquor to those below the age of 23. Family wants murder charges invoked against Suhail The family of Devika, one of the three victims of the car crash, demanded that murder charges be invoked against the 19-year-old driver instead of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. news.story_lead: Iran security chief speaks to NSA Ajit Doval on call, discusses ‘issues of mutual interest’ The two leaders exchanged views on the latest regional and international developments and issues of mutual interest to the two countries. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and his Iranian counterpart Mohsen Rezaei discussed regional and international developments and bilateral ties on Monday against the backdrop of a flare-up in hostilities in West Asia. India has maintained a delicate balance in its ties with Iran and key players in West Asia, urging for a return to dialogue and diplomacy to end the conflict and opposing all attacks on merchant shipping and civilian infrastructure.
news.full_article_text: Iran security chief speaks to NSA Ajit Doval on call, discusses ‘issues of mutual interest’ The two leaders exchanged views on the latest regional and international developments and issues of mutual interest to the two countries. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and his Iranian counterpart Mohsen Rezaei discussed regional and international developments and bilateral ties on Monday against the backdrop of a flare-up in hostilities in West Asia. India has maintained a delicate balance in its ties with Iran and key players in West Asia, urging for a return to dialogue and diplomacy to end the conflict and opposing all attacks on merchant shipping and civilian infrastructure. Rezaei, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of Iran, held a phone conversation with Doval and exchanged views on the “latest regional and international developments and issues of mutual interest to the two countries”, the Iranian embassy said on social media without giving details. There was no readout on the conversation from the Indian side. The conversation came two days after an Indian national was killed and 10 others injured in an attack on the international airport in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh by Iran-backed Houthi rebels, and a day after attacks on two merchant vessels with Indian crew members near the Strait of Hormuz. Two Indian seafarers were reported missing after a drone attack on MT Petrol Dolphin. During a meeting on the margins of the Brics Summit in New Delhi last month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian to resolve the West Asia conflict through dialogue, and sought continued efforts to ensure freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers. The two leaders discussed recent developments in West Asia, and the external affairs ministry said in a readout that Modi reiterated India’s “consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy”. The Indian side has grappled with striking a balance between its historic ties with Iran and its expressions of solidarity with Gulf Arab states, which have repeatedly been targeted by the Iranian military for housing US military bases. The Indian side has also been irked by Iranian attacks on merchant vessels near the Strait of Hormuz that have killed and injured Indian seafarers. Eleven seafarers are among the 18 Indians killed so far in the West Asia conflict, which was triggered by attacks by Israel and the US on Iran in February. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. news.story_lead: Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday - Published 12 October 2026, 07:42 BST Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend.
news.full_article_text: Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday - Published 12 October 2026, 07:42 BST Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi submitted a petition to the court challenging the process, in which tens of millions of names have been struck off the voter rolls. Opposition parties allege the revision benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. For weeks requests to protest had been denied by police, citing law and order reasons. Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained in Delhi. Gandhi called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march. In a press conference, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to Chief Justice Surya Kant, laying out their concerns with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged conduct. After they filed their petition later in the day, Kant responded by saying the matter was already before the court and therefore sub judice - meaning he could not speak about it. But he added: "You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law." There was a heavy security deployment in central Delhi and along the route of the march, with restrictions on traffic and on entry and exit at some metro stations. A bus carrying Gandhi and other opposition leaders made its way to the court from Barakamba road. Supporters waved flags and chanted his name as the Congress MP and others waved through the windows. Seated a few rows behind him was Neha Bora, a student leader who has gained prominence in the protests. A few kilometres on, in a place called Mandi House, the bus stopped and Rahul Gandhi and a few others climbed on top of the vehicle to wave at supporters lining up the street in the thousands. Many protesters climbed on to other buses parked here, while some waved flags and chanted anti-government slogans to the sound of drums and lots of cheering. "If they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?" one protester asked an AFP news agency reporter. Another protester called the march "a fight to save the very fabric" of India, the world's largest democracy. Protesters have been demanding the country's the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud Over the past week, top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, have been briefly detained several times while leading protests in central Delhi. On Sunday, the CJP - which is not a registered political party - said it would continue protesting until Kumar stepped down. The CJP, which successfully led a protest over the summer that culminated in India's federal education minister's resignation, had called for a march on Saturday to Jantar Mantar - the best-known protest site in Delhi where the last set of sit-in demonstrations had also happened. But authorities in Delhi imposed overarching restrictions that made it almost impossible for protesters to travel and reach Jantar Mantar - trains were cancelled, dozens of metro stations were shut and tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were on the roads to detain protesters. The Home Ministry has now announced demonstrations will no longer be permitted at Jantar Mantar. Three other sites have been listed as alternatives should permission be granted. Monday's demonstrations come after thousands were detained over the weekend The CJP leaders - founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - were dramatically detained from a plane as they landed in Delhi to join the weekend protest. They were only released a day later - while Dipke returned home to attend his grandmother's funeral, Das and Ranka held a press conference where they said the protests would continue. Both leaders have said they will seek a new protest date from the police. Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses. The BBC also captured footage , external of a policeman slapping a detained protester inside a bus. The Delhi police did not respond to questions about the use of violence against protesters. In a statement, Reporters Without Borders condemned the detention of at least 16 Indian journalists. "Covering events of public interest is not a crime. It is their job. The police's actions against the press are unacceptable," it said. Rahul Gandhi said that young Indians who had come to peacefully protest with "love in their hearts, not hatred or anger" had been beaten up. BJP President Nitin Nabin accused opposition parties and the CJP of trying to destabilise India "at the behest of foreign forces" without elaborating on who the forces were. Related topics

news.full_article_text: ‘Pause SIR, hold independent audit of voter deletion’: INDIA bloc petition to Supreme Court lists 10 requests The petition raises concerns over the “unilateral and arbitrary exercise” of the election body's collective powers by CEC during the ongoing SIR. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, along with 10 INDIA bloc leaders, filed a petition in the Supreme Court on Monday against the Election Commission of India (ECI) on issues linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and alleged poll irregularities. As Gandhi could not reach the Supreme Court to file the petition in person, his advocate, S Prasanna, filed it, naming the ECI, Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, and the two other election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, as respondents. What the INDIA bloc petition says The petition raises concerns over the “unilateral and arbitrary exercise” of the election body's collective powers by CEC Gyanesh Kumar during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the integrity of the electoral process, and the alleged infringement of eligible citizens’ constitutional right to register as voters and exercise their right to vote. Here are the key points: Suspend ongoing SIR until the issues raised are considered Deep Dive It directs the ECI to suspend the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls across the States of the Union until the issues raised in the petition are considered and decided, to protect the rights of eligible voters and preserve the integrity of the electoral process. Petition seeks SIR decision records, ECINET and ERONET access logs The petition seeks a directive to the Election Commission of India (ECI) to place on record the complete files, agendas, minutes, notings and objections relating to each disputed decision concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. It also seeks the relevant ECINET and ERONET access logs and the complete file recording the decision dated June 24, 2025, to commence the SIR across the country, in furtherance of the rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 19 and 21, read with Article 324 of the Constitution of India. Review SIR decisions under Article 324 and relevant law The petition seeks a review of whether the disputed SIR decisions comply with Article 324 of the Constitution, Section 18 of the 2023 Act governing the Election Commissioners, and the Supreme Court’s ruling in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India. It also seeks to have any decisions found to be unlawful quashed or set aside. Action against those responsible The petition also seeks against those responsible for violating the constitutional or statutory provisions governing the preparation and revision of electoral rolls, including Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. ECI decisions on SIR to be recorded The petition also seeks a direction to the Election Commission to ensure that every decision of the Election Commission relating to the Special Intensive Revision is taken and duly minuted in accordance with Section 18 of the 2023 Act. Ensure compliance of Form 6 with prescribed rules The petition directs the commission to ensure that the online Form 6 conforms to the form prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, unless and until the said Rules are lawfully amended in accordance with the applicable procedure. Constitute independent committee The petition also seeks the constitution of an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with technical experts and other eminent citizens, to audit voter deletions and modifications during the SIR, as well as access to and changes made to electoral-roll databases, including ECINET and ERONET. It further seeks a review of decisions, policies, procedures and technical systems relating to Electronic Voting Machines, in line with global best practices to ensure free and fair elections. Directive to issue booth-wise list of deleted voters, reasons for deletion and restoration The petition also seeks the election commission to publish booth-wise lists of all voters deleted during the SIR, along with the reasons for each deletion and a gender- and age-wise breakdown, and to provide an effective mechanism for restoring the names of eligible voters to the electoral rolls. Notice before voter deletions, inclusion deadline for eligible voters in poll-bound states The petition further seeks a direction that no voter’s name be deleted from the electoral rolls without prior notice and a reasonable opportunity of hearing in accordance with law. It also seeks to ensure that eligible persons in Punjab and other poll-bound states are permitted to apply for inclusion in the electoral rolls until the last date allowed by law. Petition seeks any other relief to protect electoral integrity and voting rights Lastly, it is prayed that this court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case, in order to protect the integrity of the electoral process and the right of every eligible citizen to vote. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. news.story_lead: RV Arlekar named Tamil Nadu governor, Kerala gets Om Prakash Mathur as President Murmu makes fresh appointments President Droupadi Murmu on Monday made fresh appointments for governors of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Sikkim and Uttarakhand. President Droupadi Murmu made fresh appointments of governors of six states – Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Sikkim, Karnataka, Uttarakhand and Odisha – on Monday. RV Arlekar has been named as the Governor of Tamil Nadu, while Prakash Mathur, who was the governor of Sikkim, has been appointed the Governor of Kerala after President Murmu made fresh appointments.

RV Arlekar has been named as the Governor of Tamil Nadu, while Prakash Mathur, who was the governor of Sikkim, has been appointed the Governor of Kerala after President Murmu made fresh appointments.
